data.source: Statens vegvesen hourly directional counts (training set)

limitation: Measured on Norwegian streets. Gothenburg is not in this sample, which is exactly why the deployed model shrinks its predictions toward 50/50 (lambda = 0.256).
question: Does adding day-of-week to the direction-split model buy anything, and should the model be applied to all six sensors?

verdict.apply_to_all_sensors: STILL WORTH DOING, and independent of the weekday question. It is what gives the five single-direction stations an opposite carriageway at all.
verdict.control: The measurement does detect real signal: time-of-day spread is 10x the weekday spread, so a null weekday result is not an artifact of the method.
verdict.deeper_finding: Direction split behaves as a near-constant property of a street rather than a time-varying one. Even time-of-day only moves it 2.5 pp, and the median station shows a 0.000 AM-vs-PM reversal.
verdict.weekday: NOT WORTH ADDING. The weekday effect is 0.003 (0.3 pp) against a reported model interval of 0.078-0.236 (7.8-23.6 pp) -- 25x to 75x smaller than the uncertainty already declared, so it would be invisible. Splitting Mon-Fri also cuts support per cell from 20 observations to 4, which makes the q10/q90 tails noisier. Expected net effect: worse.
